proof_equations.meaning: The frozen-drift LMC interpolation dissipates KL up to the discretization error.

prerequisites: The target has density proportional to exp(-V).
The target satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality with constant at most 1/alpha.

proof_equations.meaning: Lemma 4.3.4 is the one-step evolution variational inequality with discretization error when alpha=0.
Summing telescopes the Wasserstein terms; convexity of KL passes the average bound to the mixture output.

prerequisites: The target is pi = exp(-V) with V normalized as in the source discussion.
For the displayed weakly convex specialization, V is convex and beta-smooth: 0 <= Hessian V <= beta I.
The initial law has finite W2 distance to the target.
The output is the uniform mixture of the first N LMC marginal laws, not just the final iterate.
